recommendations: Run d01 to d19 in outline order, playlist numbers 61 to 79, after n07 (60). d06 is designed as d06a and d06b (both 66) by ruling 8's test (status file open question 16). Every design fits under 570 s (about 497 to 515 s).

One investigation runs through the strand (Year 11 sleep on school nights and where phones charge): d01 poses the question for the 200 Year 11 students at our school; d02 makes the survey fair; d03 chooses a stratified sample of 20 (14 nearby, 6 bus); d04 judges the headline; d05 classifies the record sheet; d06a and d06b group a class of 30's screen times; d07 graphs phone location; d08 to d10 read and judge displays; d11 to d19 analyse the 20 sleep values (sorted: 3, 5.5, 6, 6, 6.5, 6.5, 7, 7, 7, 7.5, 7.5, 7.5, 7.5, 8, 8, 8, 8.5, 8.5, 9, 9.5; phone in bedroom 12, elsewhere 8).

Joins: d01 opens on n07's final frame exactly (the survey phone; n07's provisional mark lifted 24 Nov 2026). Each later video opens on the previous video's final frame. d19 closes the strand and Year 11 ('Data analysis: done', 'Year 11: done') and hands to Year 12 Standard's first video, math-s12-a01, by showing a01's cold-open picture (the driving-school car and two quote cards).

Each 'Next' chip quotes the next video's on-screen heading: d01 'Statistical investigations'; d02 'Privacy, bias and ethics'; d03 'Sampling methods'; d04 'Faults in data collection'; d05 'Types of data'; d06a 'Grouping data'; d06b 'Cumulative frequency'; d07 'Choosing a graph'; d08 'Reading statistical graphs'; d09 'The shape of a distribution'; d10 'Infographics and misleading graphs'; d11 'Mean, median and mode'; d12 'Choosing a measure of centre'; d13 'Range and standard deviation'; d14 'Comparing datasets'; d15 'Quartiles and the IQR'; d16 'Box plots'; d17 'Parallel box plots'; d18 'Clusters, gaps and outliers'; d19 'The effect of an outlier'; d19's final chip 'Next: Year 12, simultaneous equations'.

Strand colour roles (fixed d01 to d19): data values, dots and raw answers blue; counts, frequencies, tallies, bars and percentages olive; the mean teal (a triangle); the median and quartiles violet; the mode an olive ring; spread (range, IQR, standard deviation brackets) and outlier fences amber; survey wording, categories and labels violet; answer green; mistake red (crossed slips only).

Recurring models introduced once: the investigation strip (d01; a mini strip under the header after); the dot field (d01; filter d02; sampler d03); the answer sorter (d01); the lean gauge (d02); the random allocator and fault map (d04); the record sheet and type tree (d05; graph chooser d07); the tally board and class-width slider (d06a); the staircase and reading guide (d06b); the column graph with ordinal lock and two-way table (d07); the stem-and-leaf plot, dot plot, time line graph and sector-to-bar unroll (d07, d08); the mirror fold, shape slider and peak counter (d09); the infographic poster, axis slider and icon scaler (d09, d10); the balance beam and order strip (d11); the drag-the-extreme dot plot and claim gallery (d12); deviation arms gathering into σ and the calculator's σx line (d13); the two-group spreadsheet summary and comparison board (d14); the halving fold and range-IQR slider (d15); the box build and quarter slide (d16); the scale snap and comparison lenses (d17); the cluster finder and fence builder (d18); the six-readout drag and sorting board (d19).

Memory aids introduced once: d01 'Plain words. One idea. A clear time. A box for every answer.'; d02 'Ask only what you need. Keep it safe. Ask it fairly. Make it fit everyone.'; d03 'Random gives everyone the same chance. Stratified keeps the groups in proportion.'; d04 'Check the question, the people, the method, the recording and the claim.'; d05 'Count it or measure it: numerical. Name it: categorical.'; d06a 'Group it, tally it, draw it: bars touch for numbers.'; d06b 'Cumulative: keep a running total, and plot it at the end of each class.'; d07 'Name the data type first, then choose the graph.'; d08 'Key, value, count, compare, say it.'; d09 'The tail tells the skew.'; d10 'Check the axis, the area, the sample and the claim.'; d11 'Mean shares, median middles, mode is most.'; d12 'Skewed or extreme values: median. Symmetric: mean. Categories: mode.'; d13 'σ: how far values usually sit from the mean.'; d14 'Compare centre, then spread, with numbers, in context.'; d15 'Halve, then halve again.'; d16 'Five numbers, one box, two whiskers.'; d17 'Same scale; then medians, boxes, whiskers.'; d18 'Fences sit one and a half boxes out.'; d19 'An outlier pulls the mean, the range and σ; the median and IQR hold steady.'

Everyday anchors (no people, hands or faces; no science contexts): sleep and phones (the investigation); a phone plan, a café app (d01); a gym, a council field (d02); a sports club, a concert (d03); a canteen, a phone company (d04); a playlist, a hotel, a gym (d05); screen time, app downloads, deliveries (d06a); battery life, a fun run (d06b); streaming, coffee sales, apples (d07); cricket, a phone battery, a weekly budget, travel to school, cafés (d08); apples, a food truck, a café, a die as a fairness check, a quiz (d09); a phone company, a council (d10); a café's coffee, soccer goals (d11); house prices, hoodies, a café's pay, phone cases (d12); buses, phone batteries, two classes (d13); phone plans, delivery, coffee machines, swimmers (d14); deliveries, earnings (d15); wickets, basketball, battery life (d16); bus routes, two classes (d17); travel to school, a festival coffee stall, a phone shop (d18); a soccer season (d19).

Prices and money values are examples, labelled on screen: d08's $200 weekly budget; d12's café pay and the site's house prices (lesson10's hook); d14's phone plans and delivery times; d15's part-time earnings; d18's phone prices. The sleep guideline (8 to 10 hours for 14 to 17 year olds) is a fact for Codex.

Facts Codex confirms: the Australian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines' sleep range for 14 to 17 year olds (d01); NSW Standard conventions for systematic and stratified samples (d03), the frequency polygon and cumulative frequency polygon (d06a, d06b), back-to-back stem-and-leaf keys (d08); 'column graph' as the syllabus term (d07); spreadsheet formulas as written (d06b, d07); σx and sx labels on permitted calculators, STDEV.P and STDEV.S in spreadsheets (d13); the halves quartile method matching permitted calculators (d15); whiskers to min and max, then the outlier version (d16, d18); a value exactly on a fence is not an outlier (d18).

No new plate: every plate used exists and was viewed on contact sheets (phone, phone dock, phone budget, wall calendar, alarm clock, exam desk, bedroom furniture, coffee cart, gym card, shuttle-run field, bus side, bus stop, calculator, tournament board, team caps, concert ticket, food truck, headphones, hotel facade, delivery bag, starting blocks, television, apple crate, apple, red die, cricket scoreboard, cricket ball, coin jar, club hoodie, holiday house, swim goggles, pay envelope, driving-school car).
